verification.migrationReplay: pre-existing updatedAt defaults removed; rerun idempotent (exit 0)
notTested: live third-party providers (LLM, Firecrawl, FSSAI, visual search)
external: frontend scan payload consumption (backend repo only; frontend not accessed)

findings.title: Arbitrary outbound fetches from product enrichment, image analysis and barcode decoding
findings.detail: Caller-influenced URLs were fetched without blocking private, loopback, link-local or metadata ranges and without validating redirect hops.
findings.remediation: Added fetchPublicUrl (scheme allowlist, DNS checks, manual redirect re-validation, max 3 redirects, timeout) and readTextLimited byte caps; all three call sites migrated.

findings.title: Login auto-created accounts with attacker-chosen passwords
findings.detail: Unknown emails were inserted with the supplied password and a session was returned; guest accounts with null password hashes were also loginable.
findings.remediation: Uniform 401 for unknown email, null hash and wrong password; login no longer creates users. Regression tests added.

findings.title: Admin role derived solely from JWT claim
findings.detail: Demoted users retained admin access until token expiry and a forged/stale claim was trusted.
findings.remediation: requireAdmin re-reads the role from the store (401 unknown user, 403 non-admin); JWT verification pins HS256.

findings.title: Frontend reads scan response fields outside the data envelope
findings.detail: The route returns { success, data, error, meta } with scan fields under data. Shared client helpers in this repository read top-level barcode/ocr/ingredientsText, so successful scans appeared empty. Frontend consumption could not be inspected under the backend-only directive.
findings.remediation: Backend client helpers now prefer json.data and fall back to the legacy unwrapped shape. New contract test locks the envelope, payload keys and absence of top-level duplicates. Frontend confirmation remains external verification.

findings.title: Unbounded bodies and 500s on malformed JSON across public AI routes
findings.detail: request.json() throws on malformed input (500) and several schemas had no array/string bounds.
findings.remediation: parseJsonBody maps malformed JSON to 400 VALIDATION_ERROR; bounded schemas enforce array counts and per-item lengths.

findings.title: Admin product image accepted arbitrary URI schemes
findings.detail: Any string was persisted as imageUrl (javascript:, data:, internal hosts).
findings.remediation: productImageUpdateSchema + httpUrlSchema restrict to bounded http(s) URLs.

findings.title: Hardcoded demo credentials and unguarded demo user creation
findings.detail: ensureDemoUsers contained known passwords and lacked a production guard; plaintext password hint was in a comment.
findings.remediation: Production early-return, credentials scrubbed from comments, demo emails normalized; seeding remains opt-in and non-admin.

findings.title: Vulnerable dependencies
findings.detail: After npm audit fix and the esbuild override: 2 critical (vitest 3.2.7/tinypool), 1 moderate (@vitest/mocker), 3 high (@prisma/config/deepmerge-ts/prisma build-time chain). All dev/build-only; no runtime bundle exposure.
findings.remediation: Updated sharp, hono, transformers and adm-zip; pinned prisma CLI 6.19.3 to match the client; overrode esbuild 0.27.7 -> 0.28.1 (audit 11 -> 6). Clearing the remainder requires unreviewed majors (Vitest 5, Prisma 7); no safe non-major fix. Documented residual.

findings.title: Chat response URLs allowed non-http schemes
findings.detail: z.string().url() accepts javascript:/data: URLs that a UI could render as clickable links.
findings.remediation: httpUrl refinement restricts sources and view_regulation payloads to http(s), max 2048 chars.

findings.title: Product-images route unbounded and leaky
findings.detail: No limits on names/count/length, unvalidated language, raw DB internals on missing catalog.
findings.remediation: Zod bounds (1-50 names, 200 chars), rate limit, fileMustExist and standard error envelope; legacy success shape preserved.

findings.title: Alternatives silently ignored invalid preferences
findings.detail: Invalid POST bodies fell back to no preferences and returned 200, producing misleading rankings.
findings.remediation: Invalid or malformed bodies return 400; rate limiting added to POST and GET.

findings.title: Expensive AI endpoints lacked rate limits
findings.detail: Repeated AI/DB-catalog lookups could be driven without throttling.
findings.remediation: Rate limits added on the hardened paths; language input clamped to en/hi and AI failures logged.

findings.title: updatedAt DB default drift between migrations and schema
findings.detail: Gamification migrations set DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP while Prisma uses @updatedAt.
findings.remediation: Additive migration drops the defaults (no data change); verified with migrate deploy + migrate diff on PostgreSQL 16.

findings.title: Weak or missing AUTH_SECRET accepted in production
findings.detail: Production could run with a short or missing signing secret.
findings.remediation: Production requires >=32 chars and fails fast; development warns.

findings.title: Missing DATABASE_URL surfaced only at request time
findings.detail: Store threw lazily, so a misconfigured production instance looked healthy until traffic arrived.
findings.remediation: Startup validation exits on missing DATABASE_URL/AUTH_SECRET and warns on missing CORS_ORIGINS/FSSAI_API_URL.

findings.title: Prisma errors leaked driver messages as generic 500s
findings.detail: Known request errors were treated as unknown errors, returning 500 with internals to logs/clients.
findings.remediation: P2002 -> generic 409 CONFLICT; other P#### -> generic 500 DATABASE_ERROR.

findings.title: Duplicate signup race returned 500
findings.detail: Concurrent or case-variant signups hit the unique constraint and surfaced as server errors.
findings.remediation: Unique violation mapped to 409 AUTH_EMAIL_EXISTS in both stores; emails lowercased on create.

findings.title: Guest email namespace claimable via signup
findings.detail: Signup accepted addresses matching the generated guest pattern.
findings.remediation: Signup rejects reserved guest addresses.

findings.title: Access tokens lack iss/aud claims
findings.detail: Tokens are valid for any service sharing the secret.
findings.remediation: Consider issuer/audience once multiple services share the secret.

findings.title: Rate limiting is per-process
findings.detail: Horizontal scaling multiplies the effective limits.
findings.remediation: Use a shared store (Redis/Postgres) for multi-instance deployments.

findings.title: DNS rebinding survived the initial SSRF fix
findings.detail: URL validation and the subsequent connection resolved the hostname separately, so a rebinding hostname could pass validation and then connect to an internal address.
findings.remediation: Replaced the high-level fetch with node:http/https using a custom lookup that returns only DNS-validated addresses (IP pinned at socket level), preserving TLS SNI and disabling connection reuse; handles Node >=20.13 all:true lookup results. Redirects are re-validated. Tests prove the socket connects to the pinned address when the hostname later resolves elsewhere.

findings.title: Binary fetches trusted Content-Length
findings.detail: Image/barcode downloads were bounded only by the declared Content-Length, which a server can omit or understate.
findings.remediation: Added readBytesLimited, which counts streamed bytes, and applied it to image analysis (10 MB) and remote barcode decoding (20 MB).

findings.title: Unbounded request bodies and form data on remaining routes
findings.detail: Handlers that bypassed the Hono global bodyLimit parsed unbounded JSON or multipart bodies.
findings.remediation: Added readRequestBytes, parseJsonBody({maxBytes}) (1 MB default, 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE) and readFormDataLimited; applied per-route caps (scan image cap + 1 MB, visual-search maxBodyMb, visual-search-url 16 KB). Global bodyLimit remains in server.ts.

findings.title: Unbounded path and query identifiers
findings.detail: Several dynamic segments accepted arbitrarily long values; the evidence URL schema accepted non-http schemes.
findings.remediation: Bounded evidence barcode (digits 4-32), history id <=120, ingredient id <=80, product-image barcode 3-32, temp id <=64, nutrition barcode <=32; evidence url now uses httpUrlSchema.

findings.title: Personalized analysis parsed the body before authentication
findings.detail: Unauthenticated callers could force request-body parsing and validation work before the 401 check.
findings.remediation: requireAuth and rate limiting now run before body parsing.

findings.title: In-repo scan clients contradicted the documented API envelope
findings.detail: Client helpers read top-level barcode/ocr/ingredientsText, while the route nests them under data.
findings.remediation: Both helpers now prefer json.data and fall back to the unwrapped shape. New contract test asserts the envelope and payload keys, and that top-level duplicates are absent.

findings.title: Unbounded catalog search
findings.detail: Catalog list/search lacked rate limiting and accepted unbounded q/category/page values.
findings.remediation: Rate limits added; q <=120, category <=80, page <=10000.

residualRisk: FG-04 frontend scan payload consumption is external; backend envelope is documented and tested.
FG-08 dev/build dependency advisories require Vitest and Prisma major upgrades.
Migrations verified on PostgreSQL 16 only; production server version unverified.
Live third-party providers were not called; validation/timeout/fail-closed paths are tested.
npm ci was not re-run after the final lockfile state; the existing install passed typecheck, tests and build.

conditions: Run prisma migrate deploy against staging first.
Frontend owner confirms the scan data.* contract before a matching frontend release.
recommendation.rationale: No confirmed open critical or high backend code vulnerability remains. Residual high-severity items are dev/build dependency advisories and the externally unverified frontend consumer.
